english: Among all the ancient tomes and scriptures - each holding a world of knowledge inside - the one you seek is here right on the ground.
Tingling teal cover. Golden pages. An esoteric gem upon the latch. It almost blinds you with its radiance.
Book_of_the_Mind,_Sixth_Edition
It's large, in both width and thickness.
As well as in its content.
Tome of hunger.
Your FEAR it. You CRAVE it.
(Open the latch.)
Right away it says on the first page, in big bold lettering: BLOOD PROPERTY OF HOUSE HAGGINSHAGS.
BOOK OF THE MIND, by CIVIDIX. 6th edition.
Hm. How intriguing. This begs a most indomitable question:
Is it haggin-shags, or haggins-hag?
Ah.
Hagginshags. Of course. It must be a century old.
Huh. Look at the ink.
Looks pretty modern, doesn't it?
Hm.
An interesting observation.
Won't you look at that...
The book Appledent wanted. Quest complete.
Or rather, he wants to see the sizable foreword, taking up the first dozen pages of the book.
The scholar will be glad once you deliver it.
If the upper class could be encapsulated into a single tome, I think it'd look like that.
I feel unworthy.
This was easy. Too easy. (Look around.)
(Just leave.)
Eh. Maybe. Or covered in the blood of the working class.
IT IS THE WAY IT IS MEANT TO BE.
YOU ARE.
Hold on. There's something...
What's up?
YOU WILL CEASE.
STAY. WHERE. YOU. ARE.
A blinding light, from below- shooting into the endless above.
BEHIND YOU.
(Turn around.)
At the center of the strange spiral abyss, floating, your eyes adjust to catch a glimpse of one surreal shape.
A glorious, spectral delight.
That light... this is an Arcane Apparition.
None but the greatest Arcanists held the knowledge to craft one of these...
Who are you?! Identify yourself!
An Apparition. Watch out, Snell.
WE ARE MANY PAGES. ALL WORDS.
NO.
YOUR ARCA-NISTS DID NOT PRODUCE ME.
The goblin is glaring at the horrific thing, yelling, "I am! I am!"
NO. YOU ARE NOT.
WE. SEE. YOU.
I'm not allowed to take the book, I presume.
The book is mine.
I've been tasked with retrieving this book. You cannot stop me.
Sorry, I'll put it back.
A TRUE STATEMENT.
A FALSE STATEMENT.
WE CAN AND WILL.
IT IS OFF THE SHELF.
Actually, it was on the floor, I just-
THE STRING IS IN MOTION.
While the library shakes lightly at the tone of this esoteric entity's voice, you do feel there is no immediate threat here.
That, however, could change quickly.
Your companion nervously glances to you, and whispers, "You do your thing, okay?"
Interesting, tell me more about yourself.
Can you see the Strings of Jor?
What's the rarest books you've got here?
Do you stay in the same place, or do you move about?
Who created you?
Was that your book on the outside?
I really did not mean to steal from you.
M-"...What do you want from me?"
WE ARE THE LIVING LIBRARY. THAT WHICH ROAMS THE WALLS, THE FIELDS, THE FRAYS OF IOMESTRA.
BUILT UPON WORDS OF ALL. THE WORDS OF THOSE WHO SPIN THE YARN, YET DO NOT THREAD THE STRING.
Hm. It speaks through a filter. As if it is translating its words directly from an ancient tongue.
What the fuck are you talking about?
That's very interesting. What else can you tell me?
Iomestra?
TRUTH.
EVERYTHING. AND NOTHING.
THE LOCAL APPRENTICE. THE ONE WHO MELDED WITH THE STONE.
One of the eight... how fascinating. Does that mean the Askan-apprentice is stuck in the foundation of Norvik?
Such clear and effective communication.
This esoteric being is instructed to speak only what it knows to be true.
Perhaps it knows only what the books around it knows?
Something akin to that would be logical.
WE ARE ONE. WITH THE STRING.
RARITY IS A TRAIT DETERMINED BY THE BEHOLDER.
I mean, yeah, but like in your opinion.
But like, which book can't be found anywhere else?
I see.
But if you had to pick one, which one is objectively the most sought after and, in  terms of contained information, most difficult to find elsewhere?
WE DO NOT CONVEY THROUGH OPINION. WE LIVE THROUGH WRITTEN FACT.
WE HOLD THOUSANDS OF WRITTEN WORKS, WHICH CANNOT BE FOUND ANYWHERE ELSE.
YOU DO NOT. YOU EXPECT AN ANSWER.
That's true.
You're a bit difficult to hold a conversation with, ghostly library.
WE HOLD THREE TOMES, EACH OF WHICH HOLDS A LEVEL OF UNIQUENESS AND UNIVERSAL DESIRE AMONG THE POPULACE OF THIS PLANE THAT THEY CAN BE CONSIDERED THE MOST 'RARE' COPIES IN THE COLLECTION.
SIXTEEN LESSONS OF CHRONOMANCY, BY CHRONOMANCER.
THE CODEX OF ULTIMATE WISDOM, BY ASSORTED AUTHORS.
AND A COPY OF THE VULGATA, BY SAINT JEROME.
Chronomancy? Chronomancer.
Ask more. Now.
The Codex.
That is the foundational text of the Aevan theocracy.
A Vulgata? Isn't that a book on knighthood?
A Vulgata!
A copy survived?
Tell me more about the text on Chronomancy.
The Codex of Ultimate Wisdom?
Where did you get a Vulgata?
Those seem like some rare texts.
NO. ITS CONTENT IS KNOWN ONLY TO THOSE WHO CAN OFFER AN EQUAL EXCHANGE.
IT WAS THE GREATEST TREASURE LEFT BY HIMVRÂK HAGGINSHAGS.
You must seek out this wizard Himvrâk after the election.
There is simply too much knowledge to pass up here.
THE ORIGINAL, TAKEN VIA RAIDS A THOUSAND YEARS AGO. LEFT BY RODOAR DE LA GARRA VERDE.
The Whitemanes. The lionfolk must have taken it. It lines up.
What a fascinating piece of lore to uncover. Unfortunate you cannot restore it to its rightful people. Not today, at least.
ULRIC DREIZEHN. THAT IS THE NAME THAT WAS GIVEN.
That does sound like the name of a First Knight. Like from the magazine tales.
YES.
THEY ARE HIDDEN FROM YOU, FOR YOU DO NOT HOLD ANYTHING OF EQUAL VALUE.
That makes sense.
I take offense to that. Do I look that poor?
What if I could go get something of more value and come back?
YOU DO NOT HOLD ANYTHING OF EQUAL VALUE.
ONE VISIT. ONE TRADE.
THE LOCATION CHANGES. THE WORTHY ARE DRAWN NEAR.
I see. So it's a temporary popup sort of situation you've got going here.
So it changes on a seasonal basis, or...?
I understand. It's esoteric bullshit.
WE ARE WHERE THE EXCHANGES CAN BE MADE. NO WHERE ELSE.
THE MINDS OF TOULIN'CATL. THE CORD PULLERS. SERVANTS OF JOR.
Jor is dead.
Those who made you are dead.
Did your creators live here? In Askan?
The snailfolk of Askanii. I see.
JOR IS.
JOR SEES.
THE MINDS OF TOULIN'CATL ARE EVERLASTING.
THE CORD PULLERS BUILT THEIR EMPIRE AROUND THE GATE. THAT IS WHERE. THEY. ARE.
THAT IS WHAT MANY OF YOUR KIND SAY, YES.
WE ARE. ALL TEXTS.
THE WRITTEN, THE PAGE, THE TOME, THE BOOK.
WE ARE.
An esoteric knowledge bank. Collecting the written word from everything within... perhaps a few miles?
An intense magic. Perhaps beyond even that of the Arcanists.
YOU HAVE TAKEN. IT HAS BEGUN.
A PIECE GIVEN. A PIECE RETURNED.
AN EGALITARIAN EXCHANGE.
So, what, I need to give you a book of equal value?
Hold on, isn't this a library? Can't I just return it later?
Can you tell me who left this book here?
R-"I don't have anything for you."
Can I just return the book?
A PIECE. THAT IS EQUIVALENT.
And how is that valued? Do you value it, or...?
A PIECE. THAT IS. EQUIVALENT.
Helpful.
THE COLLECTION MUST BE COMPLETE.
THE BOOK OF THE MIND WAS LEFT BY HIMVRÂK HAGGINSHAGS. IN EXCHANGE, A PIECE OF EQUAL VALUE WAS GIVEN.
Hagginshags? That bloodline is supposed to be gone.
Hagginshags? Who was that guy?
...What did that guy give in exchange?
HIMVRÂK HAGGINSHAGS. THAT WAS THE NAME GIVEN.
THE PIECE GIVEN WAS THE BLOOD ORDER OF DOUG.
Of Doug?
OF DOUG.
Of... Doug?
DOUG.
Which Doug?
<shake>DOUG DOULIN DIM</shake>.
Ah. That Doug. Legendary figure.
Can I see the Blood Order?
Right. That's the Drake Slayer guy.
YES. ONE OF YOURS.
IT IS NOT WHAT YOU ASKED FOR.
Yeah, I know, but can't I browse the collection?
Fair enough. Rules are rules.
If there wasn't a strange apparition ruling over this place, you could totally sneak over and take a look.
No. Nothing.
This book must be worth a fortune. A hundred thousand crowns to the right collector? Maybe?
A monetary value, no. But in more subjective terms?
Well, darn.
Indeed.
Try to figure out an equal exchange.
THERE MUST BE AN EQUAL EXCHANGE.
I don't think this thing's going to back down.
THE PIECE IS SELECTED.
What happens if I leave with the book without leaving something in exchange?
What happens if I leave without taking the book, and I don't leave anything in exchange either?
So, basically, I can't back out of this little deal we've got going here?
THAT IS NOT PERMITTED.
THAT. IS.
For a beat, there is complete silence in the chamber.
Then the voice says, "NO."
I think you confused it there for a second.
But yeah, this is fucked. You either give it something of equal value, which I don't think you can, or we... I don't know, die?
I'd prefer not to die, he states plainly, "So maybe we can just run?"
No, there is nothing you have that monetarily exchanges equality to this tome.
However...
It's not connected to a monetary value. At all.
It is not.
While powerful, it would be unlikely that this thing would apply its own Material Break to the value on texts.
Simply because it would not keep the value of the collection intact.
If you take out this book, and then spread the secret 'foreword' hidden within, that Appledent spoke so longingly about...
Then the value would crash.
And the monetary value of the collection would collapse.
It has to be an object of... what, sentimental value?
More or less, yes.
Something that symbolizes a similar value, on whatever ineffable level this apparition appraises its 'collection'.
Which means there is only one object in your possession that would reach, in any way, a high enough level of value.
And you know what it is.
(Grab your Pouch of Holding.) "No..."
What? You've got something?
AN EQUAL EXCHANGE, says the apparition. The light at the center of the spiral growing more apparent.
My...
My Voting Card.
Yes.
Your what?
THAT. WOULD. BE...
An equal exchange.
AN EQUAL EXCHANGE.
You know it.
You've sworn to guard it with your life.
It is a symbol of your political internal struggle.
What kind of man would just throw it away?
You're not just throwing it away.
A vote is just one vote. If you get that book, you could, you know...
Buy as many votes as you want.
You're just upgrading it. Democracy isn't that important.
Yes. The vote is useless. Just get the book.
You've struggled for ages over how to make your voice heard.
Is this the time to falter? Truly?
What a terrible conundrum! (Just do it.)
You should think about this, hard. (Come on. Just do it.)
You're holding the Voting Card in your hand. On its surface you see the marks of an indecisive man, lit up on the glow of the Living Library.
Cleric?
AN EQUAL EXCHANGE. STATE YOUR FULL NAME AND THE NAME OF YOUR PIECE.
(Give away your Voting Card.)
(Run.)
You nod towards the light. It then repeats the command.
STATE YOUR FULL NAME AND THE NAME OF YOUR PIECE.
Ragn Hemlin. (Hold it up.) "Ragn Hemlin's Voting Card."
(No. Just run.)
The Card is grabbed from your hand, as if swept up by a non-existent wind.
No.
You have nothing equal.
Not even close.
Not even the-
You have no choice here.
Logically the only way to survive here is to-
(Nod.) "Right. I've decided."
(Hold up some pocket dust.) "This is my offer."
Uh. Shit.
He glares at you. He glares at the apparition.
Then he glares back at you, nodding.
<shake>RUN</shake>!
THAT. IS. NOT. EQUAL EXCHANGE.
Too bad.
I don't care. I'm leaving.
(Toss the dust towards the apparition.)
The dust flies through the air for a bit, before disappearing into the darkness of the depth.
THAT IS NOT ACCEPTED.
You sense a hint of sadness in the voice.
The voice lets out a deep, harrowing statement.
THE EXCHANGE IS ACCEPTED.
This is a tragedy. Your one and only voice... is lost.
This is for the best. Your voice... it's not worth much.
THE TRADE IS IN PLACE.
Then the light slowly begins to fade, as darkness once again envelops the spiral chamber.
Oh, man. Good job. But, I gotta ask...
Why... was your Voting Card worth the same as the super-expensive book?
Cleric.
He looks at you with the apprehensive gaze of a concerned parent.
You know you can just get a new one, right?
...What?
A Voting Card. It's a bit annoying, but anyone can just get a new one from the District Office if they lose it.
Well.
That doesn't really make any sense, does it?
What?
If you lose the Voting Card, you can obviously just get a new one.
It's probably not a smooth process, considering the bureaucracy of Norvik...
But it is not that big of a deal.
Suddenly, the light returns.
VALUE. IS. <shake>DEPRECIATED</shake>.
No! The deal was done! No take backs...!
DEAL. WAS.
IS.
ARE.
It's confused. Now's your time.
Shit, shit! RUN!
You quickly slip the fancy book into your Pouch of Holding, and in the same movement begin to sprint up the spiral walkway.
As you do, the voice lets out a deep, harrowing statement...
<shake>NO EXCHANGE OFFERED. YOUR SOUL WILL TAKE ITS PLACE</shake>.
The illusionary books upon the shelves begin to crumble and shake.
Turning to dust, one by one, in a series of violent esoteric poofs.
Poof is the scientific term, of course.
The ground shakes and the world collapses, as you move...
Up the stairs.
YOU WILL JOIN THE <shake>COLLECTION</shake>.
The goblin is by your side as the two of you run as if a fire burned at your backs.
As if a fire burned your behind, you run towards the exit.
STOP.
The apparition clearly wasn't ready for your sprint.
The apparition doesn't seem to react?
It must be because you tricked it with the Voting Card! That was a great move!
Yeah. Sure.
Tricked.
Let's go, go, GO!
(Rush ahead.)
The shelves turn into a sea of dust further below, quickly catching up...
As the chamber shakes, you begin to see books behind you turn to dust.
As the voice's commands echo all around.
You don't want to leave.
Everything becomes... slow.
What? But I'm...
You want to stay.
Stay and read... the letter.
To your left, sticking out of a shaking shelf is... an envelope.
You know what it is.
Cleric! What are you-
(Just take a quick glance.)
It is a letter penned by Urth himself.
What? How is this possible?
You did not see this before.
But...
NO. IT IS AN ILLUSION.
Perhaps you should stop. And read it.
What's going on here?
What's going on here?
R-(Stop running. Read the letter.)
Resist.
You are being deceived.
The library does not want you to leave.
You must stop. Stop, and read the letter.
It is a letter from your god. Of course you have to. Just... a quick peek.
Please don't.
You shake your head.
The vision of that sacred letter turns to ash in front of your eyes.
The goblin gives you a shove.
Don't look! It's doing something weird- DO NOT LOOK!
(Keep running.)
You quickly push yourself around the spiral, as books begin to fly out of the shelf.
Many turn to dark ash, covering the path in front of you.
The goblin hops over the 'puddles' of book-dust.
Something's wrong with this shit - don't touch it!
Behind, further below, you see a wave of this ash forming. It grows. Filling the library.
The voice, now faded and far away, appears to chant, "THE COLLECTION. THE COLLECTION."
As you hear this, a tome lands before you. It does not turn into ash.
Look at it.
(Look at it.)
It says, The Personal Spellbook of Grand Arcanist Fillius Prax.
This is... a masterpiece. You must have it.
Grab it...
It is an illusion! The apparition is controlling your psyche!
Resist grabbing the spellbook.
It does not make sense.
Fillius Prax did not have a personal spellbook. Such a powerful Arcanist would simply bind his memorization mentally, spiritually, and physically.
Obviously.
Obviously. (Jump over the spellbook.)
Rushing past, it turns to ash behind you.
GO!
You follow the goblin up, up, closer towards the exit.
You continue up, up, closer towards the exit.
You are so close now. As the all the strange ashen books now pour into the walkway in a cascade of dark pages.
The Collection. The Collection, is echoing ominously behind you, barely noticeable over the rumbling of the structure.
Almost there!
That is when you notice it.
The magazine. It sits on the railings.
A magazine? In a library?
Yes. You can see it clearly. It is the Red Light. The best nudie magazine in Norvik.
It is banned in every official district.
A ONE-OF-A-KIND type of DEBAUCHERY.
Oh. That's fine, I really don't care to stop for a random pin-up magazine.
Oh. Truly?
Of course! The Towers had a ton of hidden stacks of smut. It's not exactly difficult to-
Hold on... look at the cover.
It's a special edition.
Oh. What kind of edition? (Take a look, it can't hurt.)
You glance at it. Just a quick peek.
Oh...! Oh yes!
Not this. You must not...
On the cover is a particularly sturdy-looking and well-built woman. The title says, Orcs & Amazons Edition.
...Urth be good.
Don't. Open. The <shake>MAGAZINE</shake>.
Just grab it.
It will be worth it.
You hear the voice of your companion saying, or yelling something. It's not important.
(Grab the letter from your god.)
As your fingers touch the paper, it turns to ash in your hand.
A heavy dull ache appears in your mind.
Your companion grabs your uniform and screams, "Get moving! And DON'T TOUCH THE STUFF!"
What happened?
Y-Yes... (Start running again.)
Yes.
Such knowledge cannot be lost.
Take the spellbook.
(Reach down and grab it off the floor.)
Everything fades away, as your hand seems to go through the book.
Through the book and the floor, into an ashen waste...
(Reach back, and scream in pain.)
The second you raise your arm, the darkness disappears.
What did I JUST tell you?! Run, Cleric!
Behind you the ash is quickly gaining on you.
It cannot hurt.
To just reach out...
(Grab the magazine.)
Cleric! No!
You hear the voice of your companion fade away as you touch the ashen paper.
It turns to dust, wrapping around your hand.
The great booming voice reappears behind you, sending a throbbing pulse into your skull.
<shake>YOU WILL TAKE ITS PLACE.</shake>
The sea of ash rises over your boots. Your legs.
Your chest. It is hard to breathe now.
It is nice here. In the nothing.
This is what you deserve.
There is no one here to ruin it all.
And nothing to escape from.
No one to leave you.
Nothing at all.
Suddenly a sharp pain grabs hold of your neck.
Tight and rough, it pulls you... away.
Away from the good.
No...
Away from the nothing.
(Try to open your eyes.)
You're not getting away that easily!
You see a glimpse of your goblin companion, desperately pulling you out of the ashen flow from below.
A leather strap is wrapped around your throat. It is choking you. But just before you lose consciousness again, the goblin lets go.
You're out of the poisonous ash. But your mind is groggy.
Now, get up!
He dragged you? What surprising strength from such a tiny creature.
(Get up and run!)
The flow of ash catches up to you quickly now. Like waves of glittering dark sand, each splash hitting your back causes you to lose strength.
The two of you run towards the exit.
Don't stop!
The chanting from below grows louder now.
<shake>ONE. ONE. A PIECE FOR A PIECE.</shake>
(Throw yourself out of the doorway.)
You and Snell both jump out into the City Below hallway.
You jump out into the City Below hallway.
The flood of esoteric ash coming after you, up until the exact crossing of the doorway.
At which point it is stopped, hitting an invisible barrier.
Which promptly fades into a solid wall once more.
Holy, SHIT!
The goblin falls down to the ground, letting out the occasional insane chuckle.
Another stupid death averted. You got the damn book at least?
Now for the important question: Do you have the book on you?
(Check if you've still got it.)
Taking it out of your pouch of holding, you do still have the quite real and physical copy of the Book of the Mind, Sixth Edition.
A successful library heist.
With some minor hiccups.
Never. Do that. Again.
Time to deliver the book to the halfling.
The goblin gives you a thumbs up and slowly starts to get up on his feet.
Next time, he says, pointing upwards. "We'll go to the Darrowian Library. Okay?"
E-"That was some... esoteric bullshit."
